players.product: Luna network HSMs (Luna 7 A790 behind Azure Dedicated HSM; Luna 8 PQC-ready HSM on a Thales-designed cryptographic processor)

quarterly_data.signal: Nine months 2026 order intake and sales (CFO Jeremie Papin): order intake EUR 19.1 billion, up 15% organically, driven by space and defence; orders below EUR 100 million are over 60% of the total; 29 large orders in nine months, 11 of them in Q3 (nine in defence, two in space). CFO clarified that FY2025 had 28 large orders (14 at nine months and 14 in Q4), so the nine-month count is 'times two last year level'. 80% of order intake came from outside France; France (20%) grew 47%, including three contracts for the development of the Rafale F5 standard; Near and Middle East orders grew more than 200%. Sales organic growth reached 8.1% over nine months, with double-digit Defence growth in Q3; mature markets grew 8% organically and emerging-market sales rose 15.8%, with Near and Middle East sales up 49%. Scope impact not material; currency negative year to date despite a positive Q3.
quarterly_data.figure: 9M 2026 order intake EUR 19.1 billion (+15% organic); 29 large orders (11 in Q3); 9M sales organic growth 8.1%

quarterly_data.signal: FY2026 targets (CFO Jeremie Papin): book-to-bill above 1.1x; sales 'now firmly expected at the upper end of the +6% to +7% guided range for organic growth and potentially beyond' ('maybe a little bit above'; 'we have no reason to be worried about Q4'); adjusted EBIT margin expected between 12.6% and 12.8%. Defence: low double-digit sales growth confirmed; Defence margin was 13.8% in H1 and the full year should remain above 13%, possibly around 13.5%, unchanged. Cyber and Digital: low single-digit growth for the full year, with digital more flattish. CFO: the mid-term plan will be discussed again with the FY2026 results in early March, when the company is halfway through it.
quarterly_data.figure: book-to-bill above 1.1x; organic sales growth upper end of +6% to +7%, potentially beyond; adjusted EBIT margin 12.6%-12.8%

quarterly_data.signal: IRIS2 (CFO Jeremie Papin): in September Thales Alenia Space signed a letter of agreement with Eutelsat to provide the governmental payloads for the 330 IRIS2 telecommunication satellites in low Earth orbit; a total of EUR 3 billion has been awarded to Thales Alenia Space for the programme, including orders booked over the last 12 months. About EUR 1 billion has been booked so far (some in 2025, some year to date, including a nearly EUR 500 million IRIS2 order in 2026), and EUR 2 billion should still come, spread over the next few quarters.
quarterly_data.figure: IRIS2 total roughly EUR 3 billion; about EUR 1 billion booked; EUR 2 billion still to come

quarterly_data.signal: Defence production capacity (CFO Jeremie Papin): radar production capacity in France multiplied by roughly four since 2021; radar production in Germany being multiplied by five, reaching that level by the end of 2026; effectors capacity grew five times between 2024 and 2026, with investment to grow it a further three times between 2026 and 2028 (70 mm laser-guided rocket); ammunition production capacity multiplied by four by the end of this year; LMM missile production in the U.K. multiplied by four at the end of 2025; sonars nearly three times since 2024; some military communication and jamming equipment multiplied by four; overall about seven times the production capacity within four years. The supply base is being pooled for on-time delivery and quality, and 'there is still growth and capacity expected to be delivered into next year.'
quarterly_data.figure: Germany radar production times five by end-2026; effectors a further three times 2026-2028; overall capacity about seven times within four years

quarterly_data.signal: Luna 8 HSM (CFO Jeremie Papin): the next-generation hardware security module, launched to protect critical data and prepare customers for the post-quantum era, is in its ramp-up and being tested by the company's closest customers in the banking industry; it was always expected to have an impact one or two quarters after launch - 'the HSM product is more of a story of within 2027 than immediate.' CFO: Luna 8's technology and capabilities are 'leading in the market' (company claim) and it is being fully certified by the most stringent regulators and certification companies, which should give Thales a technology-led functional advantage.

Cyber and Digital nine months 2026 (CFO Jeremie Papin): sales EUR 2.7 billion, slightly up organically; cyber up 2.5% over nine months and 4.3% organically in Q3, confirming Q2's growth, with H2 stronger than H1; the cyber sales-force integration is done; the data security posture management offer was strengthened to address risks from the widespread adoption of AI. Digital identity sales slightly down organically against a 2025 one-off in secured connectivity, but up nearly 1% year to date excluding one-offs; volumes of physical products are down, partly offset by digital solutions (e-SIMs, e-wallets, digital cards) and premium payment cards.
quarterly_data.figure: Cyber and Digital 9M sales EUR 2.7 billion; cyber +2.5% 9M, +4.3% Q3

quarterly_data.signal: Defence nine months 2026 (CFO Jeremie Papin): order intake EUR 11.3 billion, up 14% in total and organic terms, with 22 large orders (nine in Q3), including air surveillance and defence, effectors, naval solutions and a new contract for the development of the Rafale for France; demand strongest in naval, effectors and air surveillance and defence. Sales EUR 9.4 billion, up 13% organically, driven by the production-capacity ramp-up and project execution. CFO: short-term order momentum 'is very solid'; on SAMP/T there are many discussions with interested customers, and France confirmed orders booked in Q3. On the French defence budget the CFO gave what he called his personal opinion: a political consensus to increase spending, and 2026 spending at the expected level.
quarterly_data.figure: Defence 9M orders EUR 11.3 billion (+14%); sales EUR 9.4 billion (+13% organic)

quarterly_data.signal: Aerospace nine months 2026 (CFO Jeremie Papin): order intake EUR 5 billion, up 29% organically, driven by space on strong institutional demand, with seven large orders including nearly EUR 500 million for IRIS2 and contracts notably in Qatar, Spain and with the European Space Agency; sales EUR 4.2 billion, up 4% organically, including 7.8% organic growth in Q3 after one-off items in space in H1; avionics up over nine months. Lower air traffic, notably in the Middle East, had limited impact on the avionics aftermarket in Q3; CFO: 'we have not really seen an impact yet', though fuel prices and airline traffic must be taken into account for the near-term outlook. Near and Middle East: nine-month order intake EUR 1.9 billion (roughly times three, 10% of the total) and sales close to EUR 1.3 billion, up 49% organically (8% of revenue), expected to keep outperforming.
quarterly_data.figure: Aerospace 9M orders EUR 5 billion (+29% organic); sales EUR 4.2 billion (+4% organic); Near and Middle East orders EUR 1.9 billion

quarterly_data.signal: AI and strategy (CFO Jeremie Papin): in September Thales unveiled HexaForce, its next-generation AI-powered multi-domain command-and-control system for NATO and allied nations, available now and built on cortAIx, the company's AI accelerator where 800 engineers and data scientists work. On the AI deal with Gemini, the CFO said it reinforces the company's capability alongside the cortAIx expertise and shows it can collaborate with best-in-class players, giving no figures. Project Bromo is proceeding as expected, with closing expected during 2027 or at the end of 2027 and ongoing discussions with DG COMP.
quarterly_data.figure: cortAIx: 800 engineers and data scientists; Bromo closing expected during or at the end of 2027
